questions.q:
Statement-I: The south-west monsoon winds blow from the sea towards the land in summer.
Statement-II: In summer, intense heating of north-west India and the Tibetan plateau creates a low-pressure area, while the surrounding oceans have relatively higher pressure.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Air always moves from high to low pressure. The summer heat low over the land draws moist air in from the cooler Indian Ocean, so Statement-II explains Statement-I.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Before the onset of the monsoon, the subtropical westerly jet stream shifts from south of the Himalaya to north of the Tibetan plateau.
2. The tropical easterly jet stream blows over peninsular India in summer and steers tropical depressions into the country.
3. The subtropical westerly jet stream flows south of the Himalaya throughout the year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The westerly jet flows south of the Himalaya only in winter; in summer it moves north of the Tibetan plateau, which allows the monsoon trough to establish. The easterly jet then dominates over peninsular India.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the south-west monsoon:
1. Its normal onset over Kerala is around 1 June.
2. In July, the monsoon trough (ITCZ) lies over the Ganga plain.
3. The Bay of Bengal branch is turned westwards by the Himalaya and brings rain to the Ganga plain.
4. The Arabian Sea branch brings heavy rain to the Tamil Nadu coast in summer.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Tamil Nadu coast lies in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats and runs parallel to the Bay of Bengal branch, so it stays relatively dry in summer.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q: The Coromandel Coast of Tamil Nadu receives most of its annual rainfall in October-December mainly because
o: It is the windward side of the Western Ghats during the south-west monsoon
Western disturbances reach southern India in winter
The ITCZ stays stationary over Tamil Nadu in autumn
North-east winds blowing over the Bay of Bengal pick up moisture during the retreat of the monsoon
questions.e: As the monsoon retreats, the winds blow from north-east to south-west across the Bay of Bengal, collect moisture and shed it on the Tamil Nadu coast, often with cyclonic depressions. In summer the same coast is in the rain shadow.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about El Nino:
1. It is an abnormal warming of the ocean surface in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific.
2. It weakens the Walker circulation and tends to reduce monsoon rainfall in India.
3. Every El Nino year has produced a deficient monsoon in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The link is a tendency, not a rule. In some El Nino years, such as 1997, the monsoon was normal because a positive Indian Ocean Dipole offset the effect.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4; Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Ocean Dipole:
1. A positive phase has warmer sea surface in the western Indian Ocean and cooler in the east near Sumatra.
2. A positive phase generally favours the Indian summer monsoon.
3. The Dipole Mode Index is the difference of sea surface temperature anomalies between the western and south-eastern Indian Ocean.
4. A positive phase usually reduces rainfall over East Africa.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A positive phase brings more rain to East Africa, not less, because the warm water lies off the African coast. It can offset an El Nino and rescue the Indian monsoon.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q: The Southern Oscillation Index is derived from the difference in sea-level atmospheric pressure between which two places?
questions.e: The index compares pressure at Tahiti in the eastern Pacific with Darwin in northern Australia. A sustained negative value accompanies El Nino, and a positive value La Nina.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about western disturbances:
1. They are tropical cyclones that originate in the Arabian Sea.
2. They bring winter rain and snow to north-west India and the western Himalaya.
3. The winter rain they bring is beneficial for rabi crops such as wheat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Western disturbances are extra-tropical storms that form over the Mediterranean region and are carried east by the subtropical westerly jet. Winter showers in Punjab and Haryana help wheat, although hail can damage it.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q:
Match the following local storms and winds with the regions where they occur.
List-I (Phenomenon): A. Kalbaisakhi  B. Loo  C. Mango showers  D. Bardoichila
List-II (Region): 1. Assam  2. Kerala and Karnataka  3. West Bengal  4. Northern plains
questions.e: Kalbaisakhi is the pre-monsoon thunderstorm of West Bengal, Loo is the hot dry afternoon wind of the northern plains, mango showers help ripen mangoes in Kerala and Karnataka, and Bardoichila is the Assam counterpart of Kalbaisakhi.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q:
Match the following Koppen climate types with their areas in India.
List-I (Type): A. Am  B. Aw  C. Cwg  D. BWhw
List-II (Description): 1. Hot desert  2. Tropical savanna of the peninsular interior  3. Monsoon with dry winter in the Ganga plain  4. Tropical monsoon with a short dry season
questions.e: In Koppen's scheme A means tropical, s/w refer to dry summer or dry winter, and B means dry. Am covers the west coast, Aw the plateau, Cwg the Ganga plain and BWhw the western desert.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about seasons in India:
1. The retreating monsoon season is marked by clear skies and a rise in temperature known as October heat.
2. Western disturbances reach India chiefly during the retreating monsoon season.
3. The Tamil Nadu coast receives rain in October-December from the north-east winds.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Western disturbances are a feature of the cold weather season (December to February). In October, humid conditions and falling pressure over the Bay of Bengal also help cyclones form.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q: Which one of the following places is known as having the highest annual rainfall in India?
questions.e: Mawsynram in the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya has the highest average annual rainfall, as the funnel-shaped hills trap the Bay of Bengal branch. Cherrapunji nearby also gets very heavy rain. Agumbe is the rainy place of the Western Ghats.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q: Which one of the following cities lies in the rain-shadow of the Western Ghats and receives little rain during the south-west monsoon?
questions.e: Winds drop most of their moisture on the windward western slopes. Pune, on the leeward side, receives much less rain than the coastal cities, which lie on the windward slopes.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about monsoon rainfall:
1. During a break in the monsoon, the monsoon trough shifts close to the Himalayan foothills.
2. Rainfall in the Ganga plain decreases from east to west.
3. During a break, the Himalayan foothills receive very little rain.
4. Monsoon rainfall is uniform in distribution over space and time.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. During a break the foothills receive heavy rain while the plains go dry, and the monsoon is marked by wide variation across regions and years.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q: Heavy unseasonal rain with hail in Punjab and Haryana in January damages standing crops. This is most likely caused by
o: A Bay of Bengal tropical cyclone
questions.e: Western disturbances arrive during the cold weather season from December to February. The retreating and north-east monsoons affect the south-east coast, not Punjab in January.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about tropical cyclones:
1. They need sea surface temperatures of about 26.5 degrees Celsius or more.
2. They form most easily right on the equator because pressure is lowest there.
3. Cyclones in the Bay of Bengal are most frequent in the pre-monsoon and post-monsoon months.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Near the equator, the Coriolis force is almost zero and cannot spin the air, so cyclones form a few degrees away from it. The Bay of Bengal sees most cyclones in April-May and October-November.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the factors controlling India's climate:
1. The Tropic of Cancer passes through Odisha.
2. The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight Indian states.
3. The Himalaya prevents cold continental air masses of Central Asia from entering India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The line passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram, but not Odisha. The Himalaya is why northern India is warmer in winter than other places at the same latitude.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the cold weather season:
1. Temperatures fall from the south to the north.
2. North-east trade winds blow from land to sea, so most of the country is dry.
3. Chennai records its highest mean monthly temperature in January.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Chennai is hottest in May-June, not January. The moderating effect of the sea keeps the southern coast warm in winter, but it is not the peak.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q: The sudden and violent arrival of the south-west monsoon, accompanied by thunder and lightning, is known as
questions.e: The sudden onset is called the burst. A break is a dry spell within the rainy season, when the monsoon trough shifts towards the Himalaya.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q: Ladakh is a cold desert chiefly because
o: It lies north of the Tropic of Cancer
It is far from the Bay of Bengal
It receives western disturbances in summer
It lies in the rain shadow of the Great Himalaya
questions.e: The Great Himalaya block moisture-laden monsoon winds, so the leeward trans-Himalayan zone receives very little precipitation. It receives some winter snow from western disturbances.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Madden-Julian Oscillation:
1. It is an eastward-moving pulse of cloud and rainfall near the equator.
2. It influences the active and break phases of the Indian monsoon.
3. It moves westward across the Indian Ocean.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The oscillation takes roughly 30 to 60 days to circle the tropics and travels eastward. Its wet phase over the Indian Ocean can bring an active spell of monsoon rainfall.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following effects of an El Nino event:
1. Reduced upwelling of cold water off the Peruvian coast.
2. Heavy rainfall over Indonesia and northern Australia.
3. Warmer surface water in the eastern Pacific.
4. Weakening of the equatorial trade winds over the Pacific.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Indonesia and northern Australia usually face drought during El Nino, since rising air shifts eastward with the warm water. The trade winds weaken, warm water flows east, and upwelling off Peru falls.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Statement-I: The area to the west of the Aravalli in Rajasthan receives very little rainfall.
Statement-II: The Arabian Sea branch of the monsoon blows parallel to the Aravalli range and meets no barrier to force the air up.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Without an obstruction to lift the moist air, it cannot cool and condense there, so the area remains arid. The range also lacks the height to stop the winds.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q:
Statement-I: Tamil Nadu receives most of its annual rainfall from the south-west monsoon.
Statement-II: Tamil Nadu lies in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats during the south-west monsoon.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Statement-I is wrong: most of Tamil Nadu's rain comes in October-December from the north-east monsoon. Statement-II is correct, which is why the summer monsoon gives the state little rain.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone:
1. It is a high-pressure belt where the trade winds diverge.
2. In July it lies over the Ganga plain and is known as the monsoon trough.
3. Its northward shift in summer draws the south-east trades across the equator, which turn into the south-west monsoon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The zone is a low-pressure belt where trade winds from both hemispheres converge. The south-east trades are deflected to the right after crossing the equator, which makes them south-westerly over India.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about forests in India:
1. Tropical evergreen forests are found in areas with rainfall above about 200 cm.
2. Moist deciduous forests contain teak and sal.
3. Tropical thorn forests grow in areas with rainfall above 100 cm.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Thorn forests occur in dry areas with rainfall below about 50 cm, with trees like babul and khair. Heavy rain and warmth favour the dense evergreens; moderate seasonal rain suits the deciduous trees.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 5

questions.q:
Match the following trees with the forest types in which they are found.
List-I (Tree): A. Ebony  B. Khair  C. Deodar  D. Sundari
List-II (Forest type): 1. Mangrove  2. Montane temperate  3. Tropical thorn  4. Tropical evergreen
questions.e: Ebony is a tropical evergreen species, khair a thorn-forest tree, deodar a temperate montane conifer and sundari the characteristic tree of the Sundarbans mangroves.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about montane vegetation:
1. Alpine meadows (bugyals) occur above the tree line in the Himalaya.
2. Chir pine is a typical tree of the sub-tropical belt of the Himalaya.
3. Sholas are tropical thorn forests of the Western Ghats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Sholas are stunted evergreen forests in the folds of hills in the Nilgiri, Anamalai and Palani hills, separated by grassland. Thorn forests belong to the dry north-west and interior.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about mangroves:
1. The Sundarbans is the largest mangrove forest in India.
2. The Sundarbans takes its name from the Sundari tree.
3. Mangroves have breathing roots called pneumatophores.
4. Bhitarkanika mangroves are in Andhra Pradesh.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Bhitarkanika is in Odisha, so statement 4 is wrong. The pneumatophores help the roots take in oxygen from the waterlogged saline mud.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 5

questions.q:
Statement-I: Mangrove plants have special aerial roots called pneumatophores.
Statement-II: Mangroves grow in waterlogged, saline and oxygen-poor coastal mud.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The mud has little oxygen, so the roots rise above the surface to breathe. The conditions in Statement-II are the reason for the adaptation in Statement-I.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Forest Act, 1927:
1. It provides for the declaration of reserved forests.
2. In protected forests, activities are generally allowed unless prohibited.
3. The power to constitute a reserved forest rests with the Central Government alone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The State Government constitutes reserved and protected forests under the Act. Reserved forests are closed to rights unless granted, while protected forests have rights unless banned.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Geography of India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding India's forest cover reported in the India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2023:
1. The report is published every two years by the Forest Survey of India.
2. Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover in area.
3. Arunachal Pradesh has the largest forest cover in area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover by area, and Arunachal Pradesh ranks second. The Forest Survey of India has its headquarters in Dehradun.
questions.s: ISFR 2023, Forest Survey of India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about forest laws and policy:
1. The National Forest Policy, 1988 aims at 33 percent forest cover in the hills and 66 percent in the plains.
2. The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 requires prior approval of the Central Government to divert forest land for non-forest use.
3. The 1980 Act was renamed in 2023 as the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The policy aims at one-third of the total land area under forest and tree cover, with two-thirds in hilly and mountainous regions, since hill forests prevent erosion and floods. The statement swaps the two figures; statements 2 and 3 are correct.
questions.s: PIB; Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q: The first national park established in India was
o: Hailey National Park, later renamed Jim Corbett
questions.e: Hailey National Park (1936) in present-day Uttarakhand was the first, later renamed after Jim Corbett. Project Tiger was launched here in 1973.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about protected areas under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972:
1. Grazing of livestock is not permitted inside national parks.
2. Certain activities such as grazing may be permitted in a sanctuary.
3. The State Government can alter the boundaries of a national park on its own.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Alteration of a national park boundary needs a recommendation of the National Board for Wildlife. The rules are stricter in a national park than in a sanctuary.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Match the following animals with the protected areas known for them.
List-I (Animal): A. Hangul  B. Sangai  C. Nilgiri tahr  D. Lion-tailed macaque
List-II (Protected area): 1. Keibul Lamjao  2. Dachigam  3. Silent Valley  4. Eravikulam
questions.e: Hangul (Kashmir stag) lives in Dachigam, Sangai in Keibul Lamjao in Manipur, Nilgiri tahr in Eravikulam in Kerala and lion-tailed macaque in Silent Valley.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Match the following protected areas with the animals they are noted for.
List-I (Protected area): A. Manas  B. Gir  C. Kanha  D. Bhitarkanika
List-II (Animal): 1. Hard-ground barasingha  2. Saltwater crocodile  3. Golden langur  4. Asiatic lion
questions.e: Manas in Assam is known for the golden langur, Gir in Gujarat is the only wild home of the Asiatic lion, Kanha in Madhya Pradesh saved the hard-ground barasingha, and Bhitarkanika in Odisha has India's largest saltwater crocodiles.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q: Which one of the following national parks in India is known for supporting four big cat species: tiger, leopard, snow leopard and clouded leopard?
questions.e: Namdapha in Changlang district of Arunachal Pradesh ranges from tropical forest to alpine zones, so it supports all four big cats. Kaziranga is noted for the one-horned rhinoceros.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q: The Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary is located in which state?
questions.e: The sanctuary lies along the Ganga in Bhagalpur district of Bihar. The Gangetic dolphin was declared India's National Aquatic Animal in 2009.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Great Indian Bustard:
1. It is the State bird of Rajasthan.
2. It is listed as Critically Endangered by the IUCN.
3. It is found only in the Desert National Park in Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The species also persists in smaller numbers in Gujarat and other states, so 'only' makes statement 3 wrong. Its decline is linked to loss of grassland and power-line collisions.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about elephants in India:
1. Project Elephant was launched in 1992.
2. The Asian elephant is listed in Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.
3. Elephant reserves are statutory protected areas under the Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Elephant reserves are an administrative designation made under Project Elephant, not a protected-area category under the Act. The elephant is listed in Schedule I for the highest protection.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Olive Ridley turtle:
1. Gahirmatha in Odisha is one of the world's largest nesting sites of the species.
2. The synchronised mass nesting is called arribada.
3. The IUCN lists it as Critically Endangered.
4. Mass nesting occurs on the beaches of Gujarat.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct. The IUCN lists the Olive Ridley as Vulnerable, and mass nesting occurs on the coast of Odisha, notably Gahirmatha, Rushikulya and Devi.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following wildlife-related developments:
1. Project Elephant
2. Wild Life (Protection) Act
3. Forest (Conservation) Act
4. Project Tiger
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order?
questions.e: The Wild Life (Protection) Act came in 1972, Project Tiger in 1973, the Forest (Conservation) Act in 1980 and Project Elephant in 1992.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about wildlife of the Himalaya:
1. The snow leopard inhabits high Himalayan altitudes.
2. The Hangul is found in the Kashmir Valley.
3. The red panda is found in the western Himalaya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The red panda lives in the eastern Himalaya, in Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh and Darjeeling hills, where there is bamboo. The Hangul survives mainly in Dachigam.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q: Which one of the following animals is endemic to the Western Ghats?
questions.e: The lion-tailed macaque is confined to the evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, with Silent Valley an important site. Hoolock gibbons live in the north-east, the Hangul in Kashmir and the Sangai in Manipur.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about forest types:
1. Dry deciduous forests occur where rainfall is about 70-100 cm.
2. Tropical thorn forests occur where rainfall is below about 50 cm.
3. Tropical evergreen forests shed all their leaves together in the dry season.
4. Sholas are montane forests of the Nilgiri and Anamalai hills.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statement 3 is wrong: evergreen trees shed leaves at different times so the forest always looks green. Deciduous trees shed leaves together in the dry season to reduce water loss.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 5

questions.q:
Statement-I: Mangrove forests are found only along the east coast of India.
Statement-II: The Sundarbans in West Bengal is the largest mangrove forest in India.
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Mangroves also grow in Gujarat and Maharashtra on the west coast and in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, so Statement-I is incorrect. Statement-II is correct.
questions.s: ISFR; NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about national symbols:
1. The Gangetic dolphin was declared the National Aquatic Animal in 2009.
2. The tiger replaced the lion as the National Animal.
3. The peacock is the National Bird.
4. The elephant was declared the National Heritage Animal in 2000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The elephant was declared the National Heritage Animal in 2010, not 2000. The earlier symbol of the animal, the lion, was replaced by the tiger when Project Tiger began.
questions.s: MoEFCC; Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about wildlife in the north-east:
1. The Hoolock gibbon is India's only ape.
2. The golden langur is found in Assam and Bhutan.
3. The pygmy hog is found in the Western Ghats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The pygmy hog lives in the tall grasslands of Manas in Assam, not the Western Ghats. The Hoolock gibbon is the only ape found in India, and the golden langur is endemic to Assam and Bhutan.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q: The 'Save Silent Valley' movement of the 1970s in Kerala opposed a hydroelectric project on which one of the following rivers?
questions.e: The project would have submerged part of the evergreen forest that shelters the lion-tailed macaque. The movement led to the area being protected, and it was declared a national park in 1984.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment
